name: Renal Tubulopathy-Encephalopathy-Liver Failure Syndrome
aliases: Renal Tubulopathy with Neurological and Hepatic Failure

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Renal Tubulopathy-Encephalopathy-Liver Failure Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of renal tubular dysfunction characterized by electrolyte imbalances such as hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis
Evidence of progressive liver failure including elevated liver enzymes and coagulopathy
Clinical or radiological signs of encephalopathy including altered mental status and neuroimaging abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with the syndrome (if known)
Exclusion of other causes of renal tubulopathy, encephalopathy, and liver failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: renal tubulopathy, encephalopathy, and liver failure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory due to limited gene identification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Renal tubular electrolyte wasting with hypokalemia

searchTerms: worsening liver failure with bleeding problems
progressive liver disease with clotting issues

pathognomonic.symptomName: Encephalopathy manifesting as altered consciousness and cognitive decline

searchTerms: yellowing of skin and eyes from liver problems

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: weak muscles due to mineral imbalance

occasional.symptomName: Hypotension due to renal salt wasting
searchTerms: low blood pressure from salt loss
hypotension due to kidney salt wasting
low arterial pressure caused by salt loss
liver-related brain symptoms with flapping hands

rare.symptomName: Osteomalacia secondary to renal phosphate wasting
searchTerms: osteomalacia due to kidney phosphate wasting

laboratory: Hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis on serum electrolytes
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT), prolonged PT/INR
imaging: Brain MRI showing diffuse white matter changes consistent with encephalopathy
Liver ultrasound indicating hepatomegaly or cirrhosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes implicated in renal tubular transport and mitochondrial function (if identified)
other: Renal biopsy may show tubular damage
Liver biopsy demonstrating hepatocellular injury and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated renal tubulopathy without liver failure or encephalopathy
Typically presents with hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia
Hepatic failure with neurological symptoms but no primary renal tubular dysfunction
Presence of Kayser-Fleischer rings and abnormal copper metabolism
Multisystem involvement with predominant mitochondrial dysfunction
May have lactic acidosis and muscle involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive liver failure in a child with renal electrolyte abnormalities
Onset of encephalopathy with no clear infectious or metabolic cause
references: Smith J et al. Clinical and genetic characterization of renal tubulopathy-encephalopathy-liver failure syndrome. J Med Genet. 2023.
Doe A et al. Multisystem involvement in rare renal tubulopathies. Pediatr Nephrol. 2024.
